note: Lessons learned. lessons: short, general prompt-writing rules the twice-daily review keeps from graded runs (issue #2) and stress tests; every prompt build adds them to the writing step, and the quality grade checks every prompt against them (a broken lesson caps the grade below the 4.5 pass bar); bump version on every change. grader: calibration rules from Claude's own grading of pasted results, added to the quality grade prompt; bump grader_version on every grader change (runs log it in grade_model as g<N>, so grades are only compared within one grader version). Grades are 1.00 to 5.00 from g4 on, pass at 4.5. Never anyone's words. At most 6 of each, each under 240 characters.

lessons.text: Write the Task line as a clear instruction in your own words. Never paste the person's opening ramble or filler in as the task.
lessons.why: Stress test 1 (Oct 18): the filler opening was pasted in as the Task.

lessons.text: When the person gives an amount and what is already spent or used, state what is left as exact math (for example $200 minus $35.50 is $164.50) instead of writing whatever is left.
lessons.why: Stress test 2 (Oct 18): the prompt said leaving whatever is left; the number check now accepts correct money math (308ada1).

lessons.text: Open the prompt with the role line (who the AI should be), before Context or Task. Never tuck the role inside the Task section.
lessons.why: Regular run (Oct 21): role sat inside Task below Context; app 4.65 vs Claude 4.00 (role). Grader G3 now checks it.

lessons.text: Always state how long the answer should be (short or detailed, how many items, or about one screen) and what shape it takes, on its own line near the end. A list of sections to cover is not a length.
lessons.why: Review AM Oct 21: format was missing in 11 of 17 graded runs (65%), and in 6 of 12 (50%) written by a Flash model, not only Flash-Lite. Grader G2 checks length.

grader.text: If any line is broken or unfinished (a blank where a number or value belongs, a sentence that no longer makes sense, or note text pasted in with its filler), mark that label weak. A prompt with a broken line is never a 5.
grader.why: Stress test 3 (Oct 20): app graded 5 with nothing missing; Claude graded 3. Distance and cost lines had blanks left by Auto-Repair (context), and no length was given (format).

grader.text: A list of sections to include gives shape, not length. If the prompt never says roughly how long (a word count, a number of items, or short vs detailed), format is missing and the grade stays under 4.50.
grader.why: Regular run (Oct 21): app graded 4.65 pass with nothing missing; Claude graded 3.00. Four numbered sections but no length (format), and a filler line pasted into context by Auto-Repair (G1).

grader.text: The role must open the prompt. If the who-the-AI-should-be line comes after the context, or sits inside the Task section, role is missing, even when the wording itself is good.
grader.why: Regular run (Oct 21): app graded 4.65 pass after the label fix; Claude graded 4.00. The role line sat inside Task, below Context (role).

grader.text: Before scoring, check each label as yes or no. A yes needs a line in the prompt you could quote as proof; with no such line, the label goes in missing. Decide the score only after the checklist.
grader.why: Draft A (Oct 21 research): checklist with evidence (CheckEval, GoDaddy calibration) instead of a gut 1 to 5 score.

grader.text: Invented check: list each specific detail in the prompt (a name, a number, an item, a brand, a weekday) that is not in the raw thoughts, the answers, or TODAY'S DATE. Math on their own numbers is fine. Any other item makes invented true.
grader.why: Draft B (Oct 21 bench): g10 caught 0 of 2 inventions (B4 made-up weekday, B7 made-up ingredients and head count). Merges G4 into one concrete list-then-decide check.
